# Logistics Support

`customer_support.model.b2b.logistics` · vertical · parent `customer_support.model.b2b`

> Supporting freight, fulfilment and supply-chain operations. The subject of the ticket is moving, and that single fact rewrites triage. Ordering is by time-to-irreversibility, not by severity. A shipment two hours from a vessel cutoff outranks a worse problem with a week of slack, because after the cutoff the cheap fix stops existing and the expensive one — re-booking, air freight, demurrage — is all that is left. A queue sorted by severity and arrival time will handle the bigger problem first and pay for the privilege. This is the vertical where an expert's ordering looks wrong to everyone who has not done the job. The truth is distributed and none of it is ours. Carriers, customs brokers, ports and warehouses each hold one fragment of what happened, each answers on their own timeline, and several of them are legally the only party who may act. Support here is exception management against third parties, so the load-bearing skills are chasing, corroborating and telling the customer something true while it is still unknown. Every ticket carries a downstream promise. The customer has already told their customer a date, so a delay is not an inconvenience to them — it is a broken promise they now have to make on our behalf. That is why status updates that say nothing new still have value here and nowhere else. The error carried in from SaaS is waiting until there is an answer before writing. By then the window has closed and the customer has spent the intervening hours assuming we did not know.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | a shipping coordinator, warehouse supervisor or transport planner with a live operational deadline and several other exceptions open at the same time |
| typical_resolution_hours | 6 |
| volume_shape | disruption-driven rather than release-driven — weather, port congestion, customs holds and strikes create correlated regional surges with no warning |
| staffing_model | pooled exception desks by lane or region, with carrier-liaison specialists and follow-the-sun handover along the freight's own timezone |
| coverage | 24x7 across the lanes in motion; a shipment does not stop at 6pm and neither can the desk that owns it |
| automation_level | high on tracking and status, low on exception resolution — the visibility layer deflects the where-is-it questions and concentrates the queue into genuine exceptions |
| notes | Because tracking automation removes the easy contacts, the residual queue is harder per ticket than the raw volume suggests. Staffing this vertical from ticket counts alone reliably under-resources it.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `priority`, `commitment_ref`, `resolution_target_at`


> The resolution target here is set by the physical world — a cutoff, a sailing, a delivery window — and not by the support plan. When the contractual clock and the operational deadline disagree, the operational one is the real one, and a system that only knows the contractual clock will report a healthy queue full of missed shipments.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.commitment`


> A commitment in this vertical is usually a promise the customer will immediately repeat to their own customer. That relay is what makes vagueness expensive: "later today" is forwarded as a date, and the person who forwarded it takes the damage when it slips.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.escalation`

Requires `receiving_owner_ref`, `receiver_accepted_at`


> Most escalations here leave our organisation, which makes acceptance the only meaningful proof of transfer. An email to a carrier's exceptions inbox is not an escalation, it is a message, and treating the two as equivalent is how a shipment sits unowned across a weekend.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.incident`

Requires `blast_radius`, `affected_account_count`


> Blast radius here is geographic and temporal — a lane, a port, a window — and it lets the desk answer the question every affected customer is about to ask before they ask it. A port closure handled as four hundred individual tickets is four hundred inconsistent answers to the same question.
